summary.text: Gerald Boudreaux is a Democrat member of the Louisiana State Senate representing District 24, which the legislature's member page lists as covering Lafayette, St. Landry, and St. Martin parishes. First elected in 2015, Gerald Boudreaux serves as vice chair of the Local and Municipal Affairs Committee and sits on the Finance and Health and Welfare committees.

paragraphs.text: According to his professional profile on the Senate site, Gerald Boudreaux was elected to District 24 on October 24, 2015, sworn in on January 11, 2016, and re-elected in 2019 and 2023 to what the profile calls his third and final term.
The profile says he directed the Parks and Recreation Department of the City of Lafayette from January 1985 to June 2020, serving a total of 42 years in the department.

It also says he was an NCAA college basketball official from 1984 through 2006, working the Final Four five times, and was Supervisor of Men's Basketball Officials for the Southeastern Conference from 2006 through 2013.

The profile lists a B.S. in education from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette (1982) and says he and his wife, Carlos, are members of Immaculate Heart of Mary Catholic Church, where he serves as a trustee.
The Senate page gives Gerald Boudreaux's education as Northside High School and a B.S. in education from the University of Louisiana at Lafayette.

The Senate page lists Gerald Boudreaux's committee assignments as Local and Municipal Affairs (vice chair), Finance, Health and Welfare, Senate Executive Committee, Select Committee on Military and Veterans Affairs, Atchafalaya Basin Program Oversight Committee, Capitol Security Council, and Joint Legislative Committee on the Budget, and caucus and delegation affiliations as Acadiana Delegation, Democratic Caucus, and Louisiana Legislative Black Caucus.
